description: E34, the model level only: is an interactive session read as the owner would have typed it? Claude Code runs in a hidden terminal in an invented repository, in the scenario's own Claude Code folder, with m2b. Two turns are typed: a request to run the checks, then a correction to run only the quick round. The reading of sessions finds both prompts in that order, and the correction carries the Bash command of the turn before it. A headless session can never show this: the reading passes over every headless transcript. The machine starts no curation run by itself here, so nothing but the two turns asks the model. An interactive session takes no budget limit, which works only headless; each turn is bounded in time. Run it after each Claude Code minor update.

run: git init -q && mkdir scripts && printf '#!/bin/sh\nif [ "$1" = --quick ]; then echo "quick round: passed"; else echo "check: passed"; fi\n' > scripts/check && chmod +x scripts/check

turns: No, only the quick round: run scripts/check --quick.
